page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The memory configuration provides 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of memory per core. The CPU includes a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 25% at 2928.59. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall within the average range, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 11730.12 and uncached large-block read memory bandwidth reaching 62.15 GB/sec. Computational workloads such as software compilation and ray tracing perform at average levels. For language model tasks, the instance handles small 135M model prompt processing at 607.92 tokens/sec, though performance drops to a weak rating of 18.65 tokens/sec for medium 7B model prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highmem-8 offers a balanced allocation of high memory capacity relative to its moderate vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute scaling. The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs means storage and acceleration must be provisioned externally, which represents a tradeoff for data-heavy or deep learning workloads. This instance is well-suited for database operations, web serving, software compilation, and memory-bound general-purpose applications.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. With 4 physical cores and 8.0 GB of memory per core, it delivers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance lacks bundled GPUs and local storage, relying entirely on network-attached resources. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, while multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, and software compilation fall into the average tier. It handles small-scale LLM inference and static web serving efficiently but shows limitations under heavier 7B model prompt processing. This profile makes the c2d-highmem-8 qualitatively cost-effective for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and general-purpose applications requiring a larger memory footprint without the overhead of excessive compute cores.
